lines.text: A day's rain, all at once? Every drop, in one second.
lines.phonemes: ɐ dˈeɪz ɹˈeɪn, ˈɔːl ɐtwˈʌns? ˈɛvɹi dɹˈɑːp, ɪn wˈʌn sˈɛkənd.

lines.text: On an ordinary day, the sky lets go of nearly a Great Lake, spread so thin across the hours you barely notice. It falls like eighty Amazons pouring from the clouds.
lines.phonemes: ˌɔn ɐn ˈɔːɹdɪnˌɛɹi dˈeɪ, ðə skˈaɪ lˈɛts ɡˌoʊ ʌv nˌɪɹli ɐ ɡɹˈeɪt lˈeɪk, spɹˈɛd sˌoʊ θˈɪn əkɹˌɑːs ðɪ ˈaʊɚz juː bˈɛɹli nˈoʊɾɪs. ɪt fˈɔːlz lˈaɪk ˈeɪɾi ˈæmɐzˌɑːnz pˈɔːɹɪŋ fɹʌmðə klˈaʊdz.

lines.text: Now squeeze that whole day into a single second, and the sky pours like seven million Amazon rivers, all at once.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ skwˈiːz ðæt hˈoʊl dˈeɪ ˌɪntʊ ɐ sˈɪŋɡəl sˈɛkənd, ænd ðə skˈaɪ pˈɔːɹz lˈaɪk sˈɛvən mˈɪliən ˈæmɐzˌɑːn ɹˈɪvɚz, ˈɔːl ɐtwˈʌns.

lines.text: It sounds like the end of the world, a flood with nowhere to run. But that rain lands where it always lands, and most of it on the open ocean.
lines.phonemes: ɪt sˈaʊndz lˈaɪk ðɪ ˈɛnd ʌvðə wˈɜːld, ɐ flˈʌd wɪð nˈoʊwɛɹ tə ɹˈʌn. bˌʌt ðæt ɹˈeɪn lˈændz wˌɛɹ ɪɾ ˈɔːlweɪz lˈændz, ænd mˈoʊst əv ɪɾ ɔnðɪ ˈoʊpən ˈoʊʃən.

lines.text: Spread over the whole planet, a day of the world's weather comes down as a layer about three millimeters deep. About two coins, stacked.
lines.phonemes: spɹˈɛd ˌoʊvɚ ðə hˈoʊl plˈænɪt, ɐ dˈeɪ ʌvðə wˈɜːldz wˈɛðɚ kˈʌmz dˌaʊn æz ɐ lˈeɪɚɹ ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː mˈɪlɪmˌiːɾɚz dˈiːp. ɐbˌaʊt tˈuː kˈɔɪnz, stˈækt.

lines.text: Use a wetter estimate of the world's rain, and it barely changes the depth.
lines.phonemes: jˈuːs ɐ wˈɛɾɚɹ ˈɛstᵻmət ʌvðə wˈɜːldz ɹˈeɪn, ænd ɪt bˈɛɹli tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz ðə dˈɛpθ.

lines.text: So the whole sky's rain is a thin film, spread wide. A storm is where it piles up.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðə hˈoʊl skˈaɪz ɹˈeɪn ɪz ɐ θˈɪn fˈɪlm, spɹˈɛd wˈaɪd. ɐ stˈɔːɹm ɪz wˌɛɹ ɪt pˈaɪlz ˈʌp.

lines.text: Next envelope: how long to walk to the Moon?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ tə wˈɔːk tə ðə mˈuːn?
